answer: Each relay on the knoll earns an identity only after hardware records its uptime as notches on a timber ledger-board nobody can rewind or copy. The registry charges a stamping fee rising a fixed step per identity a household holds, so the n-th clone pays more than the first, and the fee is burned at issuance. Peers send a plume of signed probes each epoch; a pass failing probes stops earning, repeat failures void household discounts. Enforcement sits in the validation contract, so k identities cost k rising fees, k unforgeable counters and k live probes, keeping marginal cost linear in n.
